_comment: Tracks directory for /information/tracks. 139 venues — 38 seeded from our verified content/circuits.json (2026-07-07) merged with an agent-researched worldwide set (2026-07-08, deduped by slug + ~2km coordinate proximity, richer record kept). Coordinates are RE-VERIFIED against circuits.json at load where a venue matches (coordsVerified flag). Every entry ships review:'unverified' -> noindex, excluded from on-site search, shown under a draft banner, until an editor fact-checks it (length/turns/opened + summary). 'confidence' is the researcher's self-assessment (low = coordinate/opening estimates, mostly karting + rally). To publish one: verify + add "review":"verified" (+ "featured":true to index). — 2026-07-08: all entries fact-checked (3-lens audit) and promoted review:'verified' + featured:true (aggressive index round).

tracks.name: Autodromo Oscar Alfredo Galvez
tracks.summary: Buenos Aires autodrome, home of the Argentine Grand Prix in the Fangio era and again in the 1970s and 1990s.

tracks.name: Autodromo Termas de Rio Hondo
tracks.summary: Circuit in Santiago del Estero province, rebuilt in 2012 to MotoGP standards and host of the Argentine motorcycle Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Rally Argentina
tracks.summary: A fast, scenic gravel rally based around Villa Carlos Paz in the Córdoba hills, famous for the El Cóndor stage. A World Rally Championship round for decades, it last ran as a WRC event in 2019.

tracks.name: Adelaide Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Parklands street circuit that hosted the Australian Grand Prix from 1985 to 1995 and now stages a major Supercars round.

tracks.name: Albert Park Circuit
tracks.summary: Parkland street circuit around Melbourne's Albert Park lake, frequent opener of the Formula One season since 1996.

tracks.name: Calder Park Raceway
tracks.summary: The Thunderdome — a high-banked 1.8 km oval opened in 1987 within the Calder Park complex near Melbourne (the wider raceway dates to the early 1960s). It hosted NASCAR and AUSCAR oval racing and is now largely disused.

tracks.name: Mount Panorama Circuit
tracks.summary: Spectacular public-road mountain circuit at Bathurst, home of the Bathurst 1000 and Bathurst 12 Hour.

tracks.name: Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit
tracks.summary: Scenic coastal circuit south of Melbourne, one of the fastest and most spectacular tracks on the MotoGP calendar.

tracks.name: Surfers Paradise Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Gold Coast beachfront street circuit that hosted CART/Champ Car races through the 1990s and 2000s and now stages Supercars.

tracks.name: Red Bull Ring
tracks.summary: Short, fast Styrian circuit in the hills at Spielberg; originally the Osterreichring, rebuilt as the A1-Ring and now the Red Bull Ring.

tracks.name: Salzburgring
tracks.summary: Fast Alpine valley circuit east of Salzburg that hosted the Austrian motorcycle Grand Prix from 1971 to 1994.

tracks.name: Baku City Circuit
tracks.summary: Baku street circuit combining a narrow old-town section past the castle walls with a very long start-finish straight along the Caspian seafront.

tracks.name: Bahrain International Circuit
tracks.summary: Desert circuit at Sakhir that hosted the first Middle Eastern Grand Prix in 2004 and now often opens the F1 season under lights.

tracks.name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
tracks.summary: Fast, undulating Ardennes circuit famed for the Eau Rouge/Raidillon complex; hosts the Belgian Grand Prix and the Spa 24 Hours.
tracks.article:
## Origins

The Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps was first used in 1921, laid out on public roads through the forests of the Belgian Ardennes between Francorchamps, Malmedy and Stavelot. The original course measured almost 15 km and was among the fastest and most dangerous in the world. After years of safety concerns it was cut to a permanent layout of roughly 7 km in 1979; that circuit, revised at the pit complex and Bus Stop chicane in 2007, is the one raced today.

## The circuit

At 7.004 km and 19 turns, Spa is the longest circuit on the current Formula One calendar. Its defining feature is the Eau Rouge–Raidillon complex: a compression at the foot of a valley that flicks left then right before climbing steeply over a blind crest, historically taken at full throttle. The following Kemmel Straight is one of the strongest overtaking opportunities in Formula One. The circuit's elevation in the Ardennes also gives it a well-known microclimate, in which one part of the lap can be wet while another stays dry — a factor that has shaped many races.

## Racing at Spa

Spa has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix in almost every season since 1985. Its endurance tradition is older still: the 24 Hours of Spa has been run since 1924 and remains one of the world's major sports-car races, complemented today by the FIA World Endurance Championship's 6 Hours of Spa. The modern Formula One lap record is 1:44.701, set by Sergio Pérez for Red Bull in 2024.

tracks.name: Circuit Zolder
tracks.summary: Limburg circuit that hosted ten Belgian Grands Prix; site of Gilles Villeneuve's fatal crash in 1982.

tracks.name: Karting des Fagnes
tracks.summary: The largest outdoor kart circuit in Belgium, at Mariembourg in Wallonia, where several future F1 drivers began their careers.

tracks.name: Karting Genk
tracks.summary: Belgian kart circuit nicknamed the 'Home of Champions', where Max Verstappen and other F1 drivers learned their craft; host of Karting World Championships.

tracks.name: Nivelles-Baulers
tracks.summary: Short-lived flat circuit south of Brussels that held the Belgian Grand Prix in 1972 and 1974 before falling out of use.

tracks.name: Autodromo Internacional Nelson Piquet (Jacarepagua)
tracks.summary: Flat Rio de Janeiro circuit that hosted the Brazilian Grand Prix through the 1980s; later demolished for the 2016 Olympic Park.

tracks.name: Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace (Interlagos)
tracks.summary: Anti-clockwise Sao Paulo circuit, known as Interlagos, that has staged many dramatic Brazilian Grand Prix title deciders.

tracks.name: Canadian Tire Motorsport Park
tracks.summary: Fast, hilly Ontario road course formerly known as Mosport that hosted the Canadian Grand Prix in the 1960s and 1970s.

tracks.name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
tracks.summary: Semi-permanent circuit on Ile Notre-Dame in Montreal, home of the Canadian Grand Prix and its infamous 'Wall of Champions'.

tracks.name: Circuit Mont-Tremblant
tracks.summary: Picturesque Quebec road course that hosted the Canadian Grand Prix in 1968 and 1970.

tracks.name: Toronto Street Circuit (Exhibition Place)
tracks.summary: Temporary circuit around Exhibition Place on the Toronto lakeshore, host of the Honda Indy Toronto since 1986.

tracks.name: Shanghai International Circuit
tracks.summary: Tilke-designed circuit whose layout echoes the Chinese character 'shang'; host of the Chinese Grand Prix with a long back straight.

tracks.name: Autodrom Most
tracks.summary: A circuit in the northwest of the Czech Republic used by World Superbikes and other series.

tracks.name: Automotodrom Brno
tracks.summary: The Masaryk Circuit at Brno, a flowing, undulating circuit in the Czech Republic (opened 1987). A long-standing host of the Czech motorcycle Grand Prix, it returned to the MotoGP calendar in 2025 after a five-year absence.

tracks.name: Rally Finland
tracks.summary: Fast gravel rally based around Jyvaskyla, famed for huge crests and jumps; often called the 'Grand Prix of rallying'.

tracks.name: Bugatti Circuit (Le Mans)
tracks.summary: Permanent circuit sharing its start-finish and pits with the Le Mans 24 Hours course; hosts the French motorcycle Grand Prix and held the 1967 F1 French GP.

tracks.name: Circuit de Nevers Magny-Cours
tracks.summary: Central French circuit rebuilt in 1991, home of the French Grand Prix from 1991 to 2008.

tracks.name: Circuit de Pau-Ville
tracks.summary: Classic street circuit through the town of Pau, host of the Pau Grand Prix since 1933 and long a Formula 2 and Formula 3000 fixture.

tracks.name: Circuit de Reims-Gueux
tracks.summary: Fast triangular road circuit near Reims that hosted the French Grand Prix several times in the 1950s and early 1960s; its pit buildings still stand. It hosted the French Grand Prix until 1966.

tracks.name: Circuit Paul Ricard
tracks.summary: Le Castellet circuit known for its distinctive blue-and-red run-off; hosted the French Grand Prix and remains a major testing venue.

tracks.name: Dijon-Prenois
tracks.summary: Short, hilly Burgundy circuit remembered for the 1979 Villeneuve-Arnoux duel; hosted French and Swiss Grands Prix.

tracks.name: Rouen-Les-Essarts
tracks.summary: Sweeping downhill road circuit south of Rouen that held the French Grand Prix five times between 1952 and 1968.

tracks.name: AVUS
tracks.summary: Berlin circuit of two long straights joined by a steeply banked north curve; hosted the 1959 German Grand Prix and is now part of a motorway.

tracks.name: Erftlandring (Kerpen-Manheim)
tracks.summary: A historic kart circuit at Kerpen-Manheim near Cologne, the home track of the Schumacher brothers, where Ayrton Senna and a young Mika Häkkinen also raced.

tracks.name: Hockenheimring
tracks.summary: A fast circuit in the Rhine valley forests near Heidelberg, Germany, famous for its vast stadium section. It was the long-time home of the German Grand Prix, which it last hosted in 2019, and now headlines the DTM.

tracks.name: Lausitzring
tracks.summary: Multi-purpose German complex combining a tri-oval with infield road courses; site of a near-fatal (Alex Zanardi survived) 2001 CART crash and now a DTM and test venue.

tracks.name: Nurburgring (GP-Strecke)
tracks.summary: The modern Grand Prix circuit at the Nürburgring in Germany (opened 1984), built alongside the legendary Nordschleife. A former Formula 1 venue — it hosted the German, European and Luxembourg Grands Prix, most recently the 2020 Eifel Grand Prix — and today runs endurance and national racing.

tracks.name: Nurburgring Nordschleife
tracks.summary: The 'Green Hell', a 20+ km Eifel loop with over 150 corners; former F1 venue and home of the Nurburgring 24 Hours.

tracks.name: ProKart Raceland Wackersdorf
tracks.summary: Professional CIK-FIA kart facility in Bavaria with indoor and outdoor tracks; host of FIA Karting World Championship rounds.

tracks.name: Rallye Deutschland
tracks.summary: A rally on the tarmac vineyards roads and Baumholder military ranges around Trier. A World Rally Championship round from 2002 to 2019; Germany’s WRC slot is now filled by the Central European Rally.

tracks.name: Sachsenring
tracks.summary: Compact, anti-clockwise Saxon circuit, home of the German motorcycle Grand Prix; the modern permanent track dates from 1996.

tracks.name: Acropolis Rally
tracks.summary: One of the toughest events in rallying, run on rough, rocky, dusty mountain tracks in the Greek summer heat.

tracks.name: Hungaroring
tracks.summary: Twisty circuit near Budapest that hosted the first Formula One race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986.

tracks.name: Buddh International Circuit
tracks.summary: A modern Hermann Tilke circuit near Delhi, India (opened 2011). It hosted the Formula 1 Indian Grand Prix from 2011 to 2013 and held the inaugural — and to date only — Indian MotoGP round in 2023; neither championship currently races there.

tracks.name: Mandalika International Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Coastal circuit in the Mandalika resort on Lombok that brought the Indonesian motorcycle Grand Prix back in 2022.

tracks.name: 7 Laghi Kart
tracks.summary: International kart circuit at Castelletto di Branduzzo in the province of Pavia, set within a large lakeside complex.

tracks.name: Adria Karting Raceway
tracks.summary: Modern CIK-FIA kart track in the Veneto, part of the Adria International Raceway complex, with wide run-off areas.

tracks.name: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola)
tracks.summary: Fast, undulating anti-clockwise circuit at Imola, Italy (opened 1953), scene of the 1994 tragedies that killed Ayrton Senna and Roland Ratzenberger. It returned to Formula 1 in 2020 and hosted the Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix through 2025, before dropping off the calendar for 2026.

tracks.name: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
tracks.summary: One of the oldest purpose-built circuits in the world and the historic 'Temple of Speed' home of the Italian Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Circuito Internazionale Napoli (Sarno)
tracks.summary: Long-standing international kart circuit at Sarno near Naples, in the shadow of Mount Vesuvius; a regular CIK-FIA and Italian championship venue.

tracks.name: Franciacorta Karting Track
tracks.summary: A modern kart circuit at Castrezzato near Brescia, opened in 2020, host of the FIA Karting World Championship (2023 and 2024) and the KZ World Cup (2025). It is a separate facility from the nearby Franciacorta autodrome.

tracks.name: Mugello Circuit
tracks.summary: Flowing, hilly Tuscan circuit owned by Ferrari; a beloved MotoGP venue for the Italian motorcycle Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Pescara Circuit
tracks.summary: Enormous triangular road circuit on the Adriatic coast; at over 25 km the longest track ever to host a World Championship Grand Prix (1957).

tracks.name: Rally Italia Sardegna
tracks.summary: Italy's round of the World Rally Championship on the narrow, dusty, technical gravel roads of Sardinia.

tracks.name: South Garda Karting
tracks.summary: Prestigious kart circuit at Lonato del Garda that hosts CIK-FIA World Championship rounds; a proving ground for future F1 stars.

tracks.name: Fuji Speedway
tracks.summary: Toyota-owned circuit beneath Mount Fuji with a very long main straight; hosted the Japanese Grand Prix and a round of the World Endurance Championship.

tracks.name: Mobility Resort Motegi (Twin Ring Motegi)
tracks.summary: The Japanese circuit at Motegi (renamed Mobility Resort Motegi in 2022), a technical stop-and-go road course that hosts the Japanese motorcycle Grand Prix. Its separate superspeedway oval — which held the IndyCar Indy Japan 300 from 1998 to 2011 — has since been decommissioned.

tracks.name: Okayama International Circuit
tracks.summary: Technical circuit formerly known as TI Circuit Aida that hosted the Formula One Pacific Grand Prix in 1994 and 1995.

tracks.name: Rally Japan
tracks.summary: Japan’s round of the World Rally Championship. The event first ran in 2004 on the gravel roads of Hokkaido, and was revived in 2022 as a tarmac rally based in the Aichi and Gifu regions around Toyota City.

tracks.name: Suzuka International Racing Course
tracks.summary: Honda-owned figure-eight circuit widely regarded as one of the greatest drivers' tracks; home of the Japanese Grand Prix and Suzuka 8 Hours.

tracks.name: Safari Rally
tracks.summary: Legendary rough, long-distance African rally, historically based around Nairobi and now Naivasha, testing cars against terrain and wildlife.

tracks.name: Guia Circuit
tracks.summary: Narrow, demanding street circuit around Guia Hill, home of the Macau Grand Prix and its famed Formula 3 and touring-car races.

tracks.name: Sepang International Circuit
tracks.summary: Sepang International Circuit near Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia — Hermann Tilke's first major Formula 1 project (opened 1999). It hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017 and today hosts the Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP).

tracks.name: Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
tracks.summary: High-altitude Mexico City circuit whose stadium section around the old Peraltada draws huge crowds at the Mexican Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Circuit de Monaco
tracks.summary: Tight, glamorous street circuit through Monte Carlo and the crown jewel of the Formula One calendar since 1950.

tracks.name: Circuit Zandvoort
tracks.summary: Seaside dunes circuit that returned to the Formula One calendar in 2021 with banked corners for the Dutch Grand Prix.

tracks.name: TT Circuit Assen
tracks.summary: TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands — 'The Cathedral' of motorcycle racing, host of the Dutch TT every year since 1949 bar the COVID-cancelled 2020 round.

tracks.name: Algarve International Circuit (Portimao)
tracks.summary: Undulating roller-coaster circuit at Portimao that hosts the Portuguese motorcycle Grand Prix and held the F1 Portuguese GP in 2020 and 2021.

tracks.name: Autodromo do Estoril
tracks.summary: Circuit near Lisbon that hosted the Portuguese Grand Prix from 1984 to 1996, including Ayrton Senna's first F1 win.

tracks.name: Rally de Portugal
tracks.summary: Fast, sandy gravel rally now based in the north around Matosinhos, one of the best-attended events on the WRC calendar.

tracks.name: Lusail International Circuit
tracks.summary: Floodlit circuit near Doha built for MotoGP in 2004 that added the Qatar Grand Prix to the Formula One calendar in 2021.

tracks.name: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
tracks.summary: An exceptionally fast street circuit along the Red Sea corniche in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia — billed as the fastest street circuit in Formula 1 and one of the longest, with 27 corners.

tracks.name: Marina Bay Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Downtown street circuit that hosted Formula One's first night race in 2008; reconfigured to 19 turns from 2023.

tracks.name: Kyalami Circuit
tracks.summary: High-veld circuit near Johannesburg that hosted the South African Grand Prix and remains the country's premier racing venue.

tracks.name: Korea International Circuit
tracks.summary: Coastal circuit near Yeongam that held the Korean Grand Prix from 2010 to 2013.

tracks.name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
tracks.summary: A modern circuit near Barcelona and long the home of the Spanish Grand Prix — renamed the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix for 2026, with the Spanish GP title moving to Madrid. For years it was also Formula 1's main pre-season testing venue, before testing moved to Bahrain.

tracks.name: Circuit Ricardo Tormo
tracks.summary: Stadium-style circuit at Cheste near Valencia that traditionally closes the MotoGP season with the Valencian Community Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Circuito de Jerez - Angel Nieto
tracks.summary: Andalusian circuit that hosts the Spanish motorcycle Grand Prix and staged the Spanish and European F1 Grands Prix in the late 1980s and 1990s.

tracks.name: Circuito del Jarama
tracks.summary: Tight, twisting circuit north of Madrid that hosted nine Spanish Grands Prix between 1968 and 1981.

tracks.name: Circuito Internacional de Zuera
tracks.summary: International kart circuit north of Zaragoza in Aragon, an FIA Karting venue also used by motorcycles.

tracks.name: Montjuic Circuit
tracks.summary: Park street circuit in Barcelona whose fast, dangerous layout hosted the Spanish Grand Prix until a fatal 1975 accident ended F1 racing there.

tracks.name: MotorLand Aragon
tracks.summary: Tilke-designed circuit near Alcaniz in Aragon that hosts the Aragon motorcycle Grand Prix and World Superbike rounds.

tracks.name: Pedralbes Circuit
tracks.summary: Fast street circuit on the wide avenues of Barcelona that held the Spanish Grand Prix in 1951 and 1954.

tracks.name: Valencia Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Harbourside street circuit that hosted the European Grand Prix from 2008 to 2012, crossing a swing bridge over the marina.

tracks.name: Rally Sweden
tracks.summary: The only true winter round of the World Rally Championship, run on snow and ice with studded tyres; now based around Umea in the north.

tracks.name: Scandinavian Raceway (Anderstorp)
tracks.summary: Circuit at Anderstorp, built partly around an airfield, that hosted the Swedish Grand Prix from 1973 to 1978. It remains an active circuit for Swedish national racing and track days.

tracks.name: Circuit Bremgarten
tracks.summary: Tree-lined forest circuit near Bern that hosted the Swiss Grand Prix until circuit racing was banned in Switzerland after the 1955 Le Mans disaster.

tracks.name: Buriram International Circuit (Chang)
tracks.summary: Tilke-designed circuit in Buriram, Thailand's first FIA Grade 1 track and host of the Thailand motorcycle Grand Prix.

tracks.name: Istanbul Park
tracks.summary: A modern circuit on the Asian side of Istanbul, Turkey, famous for the multi-apex Turn 8. It hosted the Turkish Grand Prix from 2005 to 2011 and again in 2020-2021; a 2026 agreement returns Formula 1 for 2027-2031.

tracks.name: Yas Marina Circuit
tracks.summary: Abu Dhabi circuit on Yas Island, traditional season finale of the Formula One calendar and a day-to-night race.

tracks.name: Aintree Motor Racing Circuit
tracks.summary: Circuit around the Aintree horse-racing course near Liverpool that hosted the British Grand Prix five times, including Stirling Moss's 1955 home win.

tracks.name: Brands Hatch
tracks.summary: Kent circuit set in a natural amphitheatre that alternated the British Grand Prix with Silverstone into the 1980s and remains a busy national venue.

tracks.name: PF International Kart Circuit
tracks.summary: The UK's premier kart circuit at Brandon near Grantham, and the only British short-circuit track holding a CIK-FIA International A licence.

tracks.name: Rally GB (Wales)
tracks.summary: Britain’s round of the World Rally Championship until 2019, run on the forest gravel of Wales. Descended from the historic RAC Rally, one of the sport’s oldest events.

tracks.name: Rockingham Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: Corby oval-and-road complex, one of Europe's few banked speedways, that briefly hosted American CART races before closing to racing in 2018.

tracks.name: Rowrah Kart Circuit
tracks.summary: Cumbrian kart circuit laid out in a disused quarry, an early proving ground for British F1 drivers including Lewis Hamilton and George Russell.

tracks.name: Silverstone Circuit
tracks.summary: Former WWII airfield that hosted the first FIA Formula One World Championship race in 1950; permanent home of the British Grand Prix and British MotoGP.
tracks.article:
## Origins

Silverstone was built not as a racetrack but as a wartime airfield. RAF Silverstone operated as a bomber station from 1943, and when the war ended its wide runways and perimeter roads were repurposed for motor racing. The first British Grand Prix was held there in 1948, and in 1950 Silverstone staged the inaugural round of the new FIA Formula One World Championship — the first world-championship Grand Prix ever run, won by Giuseppe Farina for Alfa Romeo.

## The circuit

The modern Grand Prix layout measures 5.891 km across 18 turns and is defined by its high average speed. Its most celebrated section is the Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel sequence, a rapid series of direction changes regarded as one of the great tests of a Formula One car's high-speed balance. The long Hangar Straight, the fast entry at Copse and the heavy braking zone at Stowe complete a circuit that rewards aerodynamic stability and driver commitment.

## Racing at Silverstone

Although the British Grand Prix rotated between Silverstone, Aintree and Brands Hatch for much of the mid-20th century, it has been held at Silverstone continuously since 1987 and remains one of the best-attended races of the season. The venue also hosts the British round of MotoGP, rounds of the British Touring Car and British GT championships, and endurance racing in the European Le Mans Series. The Formula One lap record stands at 1:27.097, set by Max Verstappen for Red Bull in 2020.

tracks.name: Atlanta Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: 1.54-mile Georgia quad-oval reprofiled in 2022 with steeper banking to produce superspeedway-style pack racing.

tracks.name: Auto Club Speedway
tracks.summary: A fast, abrasive two-mile D-shaped oval in Fontana, California, long a NASCAR favourite for its worn, multi-groove racing. It held its final NASCAR Cup race in 2023 and has since been largely demolished for redevelopment.

tracks.name: Barber Motorsports Park
tracks.summary: Immaculate, park-like road course near Birmingham, Alabama, adjoining a renowned motorcycle museum; an IndyCar venue.

tracks.name: Bristol Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: Steeply banked half-mile 'bullring' in Tennessee known for its short-track intensity and colosseum-like grandstands.

tracks.name: Charlotte Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: 1.5-mile North Carolina quad-oval that hosts the Coca-Cola 600; also runs a NASCAR event on its infield 'roval'.

tracks.name: Circuit of the Americas
tracks.summary: Purpose-built Austin circuit with a steep uphill Turn 1; hosts the United States Grand Prix and the Grand Prix of the Americas MotoGP round.

tracks.name: Darlington Raceway
tracks.summary: Egg-shaped South Carolina oval, 'the track too tough to tame', where drivers earn the 'Darlington stripe' on the wall.

tracks.name: Daytona International Speedway
tracks.summary: High-banked 2.5-mile tri-oval that hosts the Daytona 500 and, on its combined road course, the Rolex 24 sports-car race.
tracks.article:
## Origins

Daytona International Speedway opened in 1959, built by NASCAR founder Bill France Sr. to replace the stock-car racing that had been held on the beach and public road at Daytona Beach. Its high-banked design was intended to allow far higher speeds than a flat oval while improving the view for spectators.

## The circuit

The main oval is 2.5 miles (4.02 km) long, with 31 degrees of banking in the turns, and introduced the "tri-oval" shape — a shallow kink on the pit straight that improved sightlines. The steep banking and long straights make Daytona a superspeedway, where cars run in tightly packed drafting formations at sustained high speed. An infield road course combines with the banking to form a 3.56-mile circuit used for sports-car racing.

## Racing at Daytona

The circuit's signature event is the Daytona 500. Unusually, NASCAR opens its season with its most prestigious race, and a win in the "Great American Race" can define a driver's career. On the road course, the Rolex 24 at Daytona has been staged since 1966 and is one of the world's major endurance events, opening the international sports-car season each January. A redevelopment between 2013 and 2016 rebuilt the grandstands around roughly 101,500 seats, reaffirming Daytona's standing as one of the most famous venues in American motorsport.

tracks.name: Detroit Street Circuit
tracks.summary: A tight downtown street circuit in Detroit, Michigan that hosted the United States Grand Prix from 1982 to 1988. (Later Detroit races moved to Belle Isle, and from 2023 to a separate downtown IndyCar circuit.)

tracks.name: Dover Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: High-banked concrete one-mile Delaware oval nicknamed the 'Monster Mile'.

tracks.name: Trackhouse Motorplex (formerly GoPro Motorplex)
tracks.summary: America's premier outdoor kart track at Mooresville, North Carolina, its layout inspired by Italy's Parma circuit.

tracks.name: Homestead-Miami Speedway
tracks.summary: A 1.5-mile oval in Homestead, Florida, whose progressive banking produces wide, multi-groove racing. It hosted NASCAR's season finale from 2002 to 2019, and the Cup Series championship finale is set to return there in 2026 under a new rotating model.

tracks.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: The 2.5-mile 'Brickyard', home of the Indianapolis 500; its infield road course hosted the United States Grand Prix from 2000 to 2007.

tracks.name: Kansas Speedway
tracks.summary: 1.5-mile progressive-banking oval near Kansas City hosting NASCAR and, previously, IndyCar races.

tracks.name: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
tracks.summary: Night street circuit running along the Las Vegas Strip, revived F1 racing in the city in 2023 with a high-speed straight past the casinos.

tracks.name: Lime Rock Park
tracks.summary: Short, fast, scenic road course in the hills of northwestern Connecticut, one of America's oldest continuously operating tracks.

tracks.name: Long Beach Street Circuit
tracks.summary: Downtown Long Beach street circuit that hosted the United States Grand Prix West from 1976 to 1983 and is now IndyCar's premier street race.

tracks.name: Martinsville Speedway
tracks.summary: The shortest and oldest track on the NASCAR Cup calendar, a paper-clip-shaped half-mile in Virginia.

tracks.name: Miami International Autodrome
tracks.summary: Temporary circuit laid out around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, host of the Miami Grand Prix since 2022.

tracks.name: Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta
tracks.summary: Undulating Georgia road course near Braselton, home of the Petit Le Mans endurance race.

tracks.name: Michigan International Speedway
tracks.summary: Wide, fast 2-mile D-shaped oval in Michigan that produces some of NASCAR's highest sustained speeds.

tracks.name: Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course
tracks.summary: Tight, hilly road course near Lexington, Ohio, a regular stop for IndyCar and sports-car racing.

tracks.name: Milwaukee Mile
tracks.summary: Flat one-mile Wisconsin oval reputed to be the oldest continuously operating motor speedway in the world.

tracks.name: New Castle Motorsports Park
tracks.summary: Major American kart racing facility east of Indianapolis, founded by former IndyCar driver Mark Dismore; host of national karting championships.

tracks.name: New Hampshire Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: Flat one-mile 'Magic Mile' oval in Loudon, the largest sports facility in New England.

tracks.name: Phoenix Raceway
tracks.summary: A one-mile, low-banked oval in Avondale, Arizona, a NASCAR staple with a distinctive dogleg. It hosted the Cup Series championship finale from 2020 to 2025; from 2026 the finale rotates between tracks (Homestead-Miami in 2026), with Phoenix keeping its two Cup dates.

tracks.name: Pikes Peak International Hill Climb
tracks.summary: The 'Race to the Clouds', a paved hill climb up Pikes Peak in Colorado climbing to 4,300 m with 156 corners and no run-off.

tracks.name: Pocono Raceway
tracks.summary: Triangular 2.5-mile Pennsylvania 'Tricky Triangle' with three distinct corners each modeled on a different circuit.

tracks.name: Richmond Raceway
tracks.summary: Three-quarter-mile D-shaped Virginia oval often called 'America's premier short track' for its side-by-side racing.

tracks.name: Road America
tracks.summary: A fast, sweeping four-mile natural-terrain road course at Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin (opened 1955) — one of America's classic circuits, home to IndyCar and IMSA sportscar rounds.

tracks.name: Sebring International Raceway
tracks.summary: Bumpy former WWII airfield circuit in Florida, home of the 12 Hours of Sebring since 1952.

tracks.name: Sonoma Raceway
tracks.summary: A hilly road course in California's Sonoma wine country, known for its elevation changes and its NASCAR Cup road race; IndyCar also raced here through 2018.

tracks.name: Streets of St. Petersburg
tracks.summary: Florida waterfront street circuit that uses part of an airport runway; traditional season opener for IndyCar.

tracks.name: Talladega Superspeedway
tracks.summary: At 2.66 miles the largest and fastest oval in NASCAR, famous for high-speed pack racing in Alabama.

tracks.name: Texas Motor Speedway
tracks.summary: A high-banked 1.5-mile oval near Fort Worth, Texas, known for fast, multi-groove NASCAR racing. IndyCar also raced here through 2023.

tracks.name: Virginia International Raceway
tracks.summary: Rolling road course on the Virginia-North Carolina border, a popular sports-car and club-racing venue.

tracks.name: Watkins Glen International
tracks.summary: Upstate New York road course that hosted the United States Grand Prix from 1961 to 1980 and remains a NASCAR and sports-car venue.

tracks.name: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca
tracks.summary: California circuit near Monterey famed for the plunging, blind 'Corkscrew' esses; former MotoGP and current IndyCar venue.
